howDoI.q: How do I make something change after a few seconds?
How do I show how much time is left?
How do I make a gate that shuts when time runs out?
How do I let the player start the clock again?
How do I make a clock that starts over by itself?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Beat the Clock is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

The bar above you is your time. Nothing in this game hurts you: running out of time only means the gate is shut.

pages.head: Level 1: Beat the Clock
pages.html:
Level 1: Beat the Clock

The level's clock starts the moment the level does, so there is a level card first. The THE BAR IS YOUR TIME sign stands under a bar of five green pieces. They go out one at a time, the right-hand one first, and each goes thin and orange for its last second. A little clock face at the bar's left end moves its hand a quarter turn every second. When the last piece is dark, a lamp over the gate in the brick wall turns red and the gate shuts.

Run for it. The bar is about sixteen seconds long, and the gate is a long walk away. If you are too slow, push on into the gate: it is solid. Then walk all the way back to the teal clock door at the start (the sign near the middle says so). Stepping into it starts the level again, with a full bar and an open gate.

There are thirteen coins in all (some come back when you try again), worth ten points each.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The only clock there is. A block can turn into another block after some time. Open one.bbl in the blocks editor and pick a block such as seg0.on. Its Next block is seg0.warn and its Time is a number of ticks. There are 18.2 ticks in a second, so 60 ticks is a little over three seconds. Game-Maker has no other clock.
  • The bar. Each of the five pieces is its own set of three blocks: seg0.on (green), seg0.warn (thin and orange) and seg0.off (dark). seg4.on lasts 44 ticks before it warns and the next piece 60 ticks longer, so they go out about three seconds after each other. The picture of each is only a picture; the bar is the blocks changing.
  • Why five sets of blocks. Every block of one kind changes at the same moment, wherever it is on the map. The game cannot start a clock in one place. So a piece that must go out later than its neighbor has to be a different kind of block.
  • One bar, four times. The same bar is placed four times along the level, so there is always one overhead. They tick as one because they are the same kinds of block. Open one.map and look at the top row.
  • The clock face. face0 turns into face1 after 18 ticks, then face2, face3 and back to face0. A loop is just a block whose last stop is the first.
  • The gate. It fills a tunnel three blocks wide and two high, so it is six blocks, such as gate.open.top.m, that you can walk through. After 300 ticks, exactly when the last piece goes out, each turns into its gate.shut twin: the same place, but with its Solid boxes checked. The shut gate has no Next block, so it stays shut. The lamp over it, lamp.open, turns into lamp.shut on the same tick.
  • The clock starts with the level. The timers are set when the level's scene is loaded, which is why the level card comes first. A level cannot start its clock later, when you reach a place or press a key.
  • The clock door. It is an ordinary door whose link in beat.gam goes to the same scene it is in. Loading the scene again sets every timer again.
  • The walls. The room is closed in by brick walls at both ends. The gate wall is brick down to a two-block tunnel, higher than a jump, so there is no way around the gate.

pages.head: Level 2: Round and Round
pages.html:
Level 2: Round and Round

The THIS CLOCK STARTS OVER BY ITSELF sign stands under a bar like the first. This time the bar's pieces go out, the gate shuts, and then, a few seconds later, the whole bar lights again at once and the gate opens. It does this round after round, so there is no clock door and no hurry.

The GATE SHUT? sign says what to do: wait. The round is about twelve seconds of open gate and four of shut.

There are nine coins on the way.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • Its own block file. This level loads two.bbl, not one.bbl. The blocks have the same names, but their times are different, which is what lets the same bar mean a different clock here.
  • Starting over. In level 1 a piece's last block, seg0.off, has no Next block. Here seg0.off has seg0.on as its Next block, with a Time that makes the whole round add up to 305 ticks. When the Next block comes back around to the first, the clock runs for ever.
  • The gate. gate.open lasts 225 ticks and gate.shut 80 ticks, then it is open again. lamp.open and lamp.shut keep the same round, so the lamp always matches the gate.
  • What you wait for. The gate is the only thing in the way, so waiting is safe: nothing here hurts, and the gate comes round again. This is why a looping clock suits a puzzle where you must be there at the right moment.

pages.head: What Game-Maker cannot do
pages.html:
What Game-Maker cannot do

A clock in Game-Maker is only blocks that change. Some things you may expect are not there:

  • It cannot show the time as a number. A bar of pictures is the best it can do.
  • It cannot start a clock when something happens. Every timer starts when the scene loads, and loading the scene again, as the clock door does, is the only way to start one over.
  • It cannot end the level or take a life when the time is up. Here, running out of time shuts a solid gate and that is all.
  • It cannot play a sound when a block changes, so the gate shuts in silence.
  • A block does not know what its neighbors are doing. Two blocks of the same kind always change together, so a clock that is different in two places needs two kinds of block.
  • Monsters have a clock of their own: a monster can live for a set time and then turn into another monster, as Throw It's star does. It is a separate clock, set when each monster is born.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In one.bbl, make seg4.on last longer, and see the bar's first piece go out later.
  • Make the gate's Time shorter than the bar's, and see the gate shut with light left.
  • Make each clock face block's Time 9 and watch the hand speed up.
  • Draw a new picture for seg0.on in the blocks editor.
  • Give the shut gate blocks a Next block (the open ones) and a Time, and the gate opens again by itself.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
